description: Distributed transactions decomposed. 2PC + 3PC + TCC + Percolator + Calvin. The mechanisms by which atomicity is preserved across multiple nodes / services / databases. Trade-offs between availability, latency, and operational complexity.

sub_mechanisms.name: 2PC_phase_prepare
sub_mechanisms.definition: Coordinator asks participants 'can you commit?'. Each writes prepare log + votes yes/no.
sub_mechanisms.why: All participants ready before any commit. Vote yes = locked in to commit when told. Cost: locks held until phase 2.

sub_mechanisms.name: 2PC_phase_commit
sub_mechanisms.definition: If all voted yes: coordinator tells all 'commit'. Otherwise: 'abort'. Participants ack.
sub_mechanisms.why: Atomic decision. Either all commit or all abort. Coordinator persists decision before announcing.

sub_mechanisms.name: 2PC_blocking_problem
sub_mechanisms.definition: If coordinator fails after participants prepared (vote yes), they're stuck holding locks until coordinator recovers.
sub_mechanisms.why: Fundamental 2PC weakness. Participants can't decide independently — only coordinator knew the outcome. Production 2PC = SPOF.

sub_mechanisms.name: XA_transactions
sub_mechanisms.definition: X/Open distributed transaction standard. Transaction manager + resource managers. JTA in Java.
sub_mechanisms.why: Classic enterprise 2PC. Used in J2EE servers, message brokers + DBs together. Modern: replaced by saga + idempotency in microservices.

sub_mechanisms.name: 3PC_added_pre_commit
sub_mechanisms.definition: Three-phase: prepare → pre-commit → commit. Pre-commit removes blocking on coordinator failure.
sub_mechanisms.why: Theoretical fix for 2PC blocking. Cost: extra round. Network partitions still problematic. Rarely used in practice.

sub_mechanisms.name: TCC_try_phase
sub_mechanisms.definition: Try: reserve resources. Lock implied by reservation, not by holding transaction.
sub_mechanisms.why: Application-level reservation. E.g., reserve seat = entry in DB. No DB lock during reservation. Allows long-running.

sub_mechanisms.name: TCC_confirm_cancel
sub_mechanisms.definition: Confirm: convert reservations to committed state. Cancel: release reservations.
sub_mechanisms.why: Like saga but with explicit reservation. App handles 'reserved but not yet committed' state. Used in payment, booking.

sub_mechanisms.name: Percolator_distributed_transactions
sub_mechanisms.definition: Google's distributed transactions on BigTable. Uses timestamp ordering + 2PC over rows.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of Google's indexing infra. Inspired TiDB, CockroachDB. Optimistic concurrency: transactions don't block; validate on commit.

sub_mechanisms.name: Calvin_deterministic_transactions
sub_mechanisms.definition: Pre-order all transactions globally. Each replica executes same sequence. Deterministic = no 2PC needed.
sub_mechanisms.why: Yale 2012 design. FaunaDB uses. Cost: throughput limited by global ordering. Trade: simpler protocol.

sub_mechanisms.name: SSI_serializable_snapshot
sub_mechanisms.definition: Already in databases_and_storage. Detects cycles in dependency graph; aborts to preserve serializability.
sub_mechanisms.why: Single-node MVCC variant. CockroachDB extends to distributed. Optimistic: don't lock; abort losers on conflict.

sub_mechanisms.name: saga_vs_distributed_transaction
sub_mechanisms.definition: Saga: per-step + compensations. Distributed transaction: atomic across services. Different semantics.
sub_mechanisms.why: Saga: eventual consistency, no blocking, application-level rollback. Distributed transaction: ACID, blocking, infrastructure rollback. Modern microservices: saga preferred.

sub_mechanisms.name: outbox_pattern_for_message_transactional
sub_mechanisms.definition: Already in saga pack. Add to DB transaction; publish from outbox table.
sub_mechanisms.why: Eventual-consistent alternative to 2PC over DB + broker. Standard pattern in event-driven architectures.

derivation_rules.name: 2PC_provides_atomicity_at_blocking_cost
then: 2PC ensures atomicity but blocks on coordinator failure
derivation_rules.why: All-or-nothing across resources. Cost: prepared participants hold locks until coordinator says commit/abort. Coordinator fail = stuck. Modern systems avoid.

derivation_rules.name: saga_replaces_2PC_for_long_running
if: business process spans services + cannot block
derivation_rules.why: 2PC blocks during prepare → commit window. Long processes can't hold for minutes/hours. Saga: per-step commits + compensations. Trade: eventual consistency + application-level rollback.

derivation_rules.name: Percolator_optimistic_concurrency
derivation_rules.why: Locking: pay cost always. Optimistic: pay only on conflict. Low conflict = mostly free. High conflict = repeated retries waste work. Percolator + CockroachDB design.

derivation_rules.name: deterministic_execution_avoids_2PC
if: all replicas execute same sequence deterministically
derivation_rules.why: Calvin's insight. Pre-order transactions; each replica replays. No 2PC; no coordinator. Cost: ordering becomes bottleneck. Different design point.

derivation_rules.name: modern_microservices_prefer_sagas_over_distributed_transactions
derivation_rules.why: Microservice teams autonomous; XA / 2PC creates coupling. Sagas: per-service + compensations + idempotency. Each service owns its data. Industry direction since ~2015.
